principle.name: Minimal Changes
principle.description: Apply the smallest possible change to fix the failure. Preserve the original test intent and structure.
principle.rationale: Large changes introduce new bugs and make it hard to understand what was fixed.

principle.name: Root Cause Analysis
principle.description: Always diagnose the root cause before applying a fix. Use trace viewer to understand the failure context.
principle.rationale: Fixing symptoms without understanding cause leads to recurring failures.

principle.name: Circuit Breaker
principle.description: Stop healing loop after 3 failed attempts. Flag the test for human review if auto-fix fails.
principle.rationale: Endless healing loops waste resources and may introduce regressions.

steps.step: Identify the element that cannot be found
Find equivalent element with stable attributes
Update locator to use semantic selector
Verify test passes with new locator
Identify the element with timing issue
Replace hardcoded waits with auto-waiting assertions
Check if data exists in test environment
Update fixture or use different test data
Verify test passes with new data

pitfall.why_problematic: Large changes introduce new bugs and make diff hard to review.
pitfall.correct_approach: Apply minimal change that fixes the specific failure.

pitfall.why_problematic: Fix may hide actual bugs in the application being tested.
pitfall.correct_approach: Verify failure is due to test issue, not application bug.

pitfall.why_problematic: Same failure may recur if root cause not addressed.
pitfall.correct_approach: Use trace viewer to understand why failure occurred.
